# Report: region.fasta (header `>region_007`)

## 1. Basic properties
| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Length | 3,000 bp (single sequence, no gaps/ambiguities) |
| Composition | A 657, C 768, G 763, T 812 |
| GC content | **51.0 %** (no AT- or GC-skew anomaly; GC is flat across the molecule) |
| Repeats | No internal duplication, no tandem repeats, no long inverted repeats (see §3) |

## 2. The sequence is very likely protein-coding (main finding)
This is not a featureless stretch of DNA. The clearest signal is a large open reading frame on the **plus strand**:

- **Stop-free region: 1028–2623 (1,598 bp).** This is the only long stop-free stretch in the molecule. For a 3 kb sequence of this composition the longest ORF expected by chance is ~170 codons, so a 532-codon stop-free run is far outside random expectation.
- **Predicted CDS: 1085–2623 (1,539 bp)**, first in-frame ATG at 1085, terminated by TGA at 2624–2626. It encodes a **513-amino-acid protein** (protein coordinates below are relative to this Met = residue 1).
- **Frame-specific stop-codon statistics support frame +1 as the coding frame:** +1 = 20 stops (depleted), +0 = 34, +2 = 56 (5.6 %, markedly elevated). Stop-codon excess in the +1-shifted frame and depletion in the coding frame is the classic signature of a translated sequence.
- **Codon usage** of the 513-codon ORF correlates strongly with *E. coli* K-12 codon usage (r ≈ 0.81; non-coding frames of the same sequence give r ≈ 0.05–0.5), and only ~2.5 % of its codons are rare ones — consistent with a genuine bacterial gene rather than a chance ORF.
- **The protein is a hydrophobic, polytopic membrane protein.** Kyte–Doolittle hydropathy (19-residue window) predicts ~10–12 hydrophobic segments suitable as transmembrane helices, clustered at approximately residues 28–52, 97–109, 135–160, 247–254, 305–330, 357–373 and 482–493 (i.e. roughly nt 1,166–1,240, 1,373–1,411, 1,487–1,565, 1,823–1,847, 1,997–2,077, 2,153–2,201 and 2,528–2,561). Overall amino-acid composition is dominated by Leu (83), Ala (50), Val (47), Ile (38), Phe (35). This profile — a ~55 kDa, highly hydrophobic, ~11-TM protein — is typical of an **integral membrane transporter/permease**. No homology search could be run here, so the specific family/function remains unassigned.

## 3. Other long open reading frames
Three additional stop-free regions ≥100 codons exist (all shorter and less compelling than the ORF above):

| Coordinates (1-based) | Strand / frame | Length | Largest ATG-initiated ORF |
|---|---|---|---|
| 148–921 | minus, frame 0 | 258 codons | **148–864**, 239 aa |
| 2285–2746 | minus, frame 2 | 154 codons | 2285–2644, 120 aa (overlaps the 513-aa ORF on the opposite strand) |
| 166–624 | plus, frame 0 | 153 codons | 214–624, 137 aa |

The 239-aa ORF at **148–864 (minus strand)** is the only other one worth noting (its codon usage also trends *E. coli*-like, r ≈ 0.76); the remaining two are within the range expected for random DNA and are probably incidental. The plus-strand ORF at 1085–2623 is by a wide margin the dominant coding feature.

## 4. Which ancillary features are *not* present
- **No duplicated/repeated blocks.** Scanning every offset, no alignment exceeds background identity (~26–30 %); the longest exact repeat found anywhere is only 12 bp (e.g. 656↔2543, 1494↔2439). No mobile-element (IS/transposon) signature.
- **No tandem repeat arrays** (no unit ≥6 bp present in ≥3 copies).
- **No long inverted repeats / stem-loops** (no stem ≥12 bp), so no obvious terminator-like or cruciform structure.
- **No canonical promoter motifs** (TTGACA/TATAAT absent). One AGGAGG-like Shine–Dalgarno at 2704 (minus strand) and one Chi site (GCTGGTGG) at 1948 (minus strand) — neither is convincingly positioned relative to the ORFs.

Small incidental features: two short palindromic/hairpin motifs, 104–125 (`AAACCCCTC`–`GAGGGGTTT`) and 2636–2657 (`ACCGGGCAT`–`ATGCCCGGT`, i.e. just downstream of the 513-aa ORF's stop); two homopolymer runs, A₆ at 101–106 and T₆ at 1120–1125; two sites each for the palindromic 6-cutters HindIII (AAGCTT, at 1026 and elsewhere), KpnI (GGTACC), SmaI (CCCGGG) and NcoI (CCATGG).

## 5. Summary
The region is **not** unremarkable: it carries a strong coding signature in reading frame +1, a **1,539 bp ORF at 1085–2623** encoding a **513-aa, highly hydrophobic, ~11-transmembrane protein** whose codon usage closely matches *E. coli* — i.e. a probable integral membrane protein (transporter-like) gene, functionally unassigned. The most notable secondary observation is a **239-aa ORF on the opposite strand at 148–864**, plus one short (~150-codon) ORF at 2285–2746 overlapping the main gene in the antisense direction. There is no evidence of repeats, transposons, tandem arrays or secondary-structure motifs; the remainder of the sequence behaves as ordinary non-coding DNA. Interpretation of function would require a homology search against a protein database, which was not possible in this environment.
